_meta.description: Ordering playbook for eating out with pancreatitis. General strategies by cuisine, not menu data. Restaurants and kitchens vary, and any single dish can be made differently in two places on the same street. Treat every line as a starting point for a conversation with the kitchen.
_meta.disclaimer: General information only. Not medical or dietetic advice. Your care team's instructions always win.
_meta.maintenanceNote: Chain nutrition links move. If one is dead, search for the chain name plus 'nutrition PDF', update the URL here, and commit. If the chain stops publishing, set nutritionUrl to null rather than deleting the chain.

universal.title: How to order anywhere
strategies: Look for grilled, baked, broiled, steamed, poached, or roasted. Those six words are most of the job. The ones to pass on are fried, crispy, breaded, battered, buttered, creamy, smothered, and au gratin.

Sauces, dressings, and gravy on the side, every single time. A dressing you spoon on yourself is a small fraction of the one they pour in the kitchen, and this one habit does more work than any other.
Ask what the kitchen cooks with. Almost every kitchen uses oil or butter by default, and almost every kitchen will use broth, stock, or a light spray instead if you ask them to.

Say it as a medical requirement rather than a preference. Kitchens take 'I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet' seriously in a way they do not take 'I am watching my fat'. It is also simply true.
Ask questions that have a yes or no answer. 'Can the kitchen cook that with no butter?' gets you a real answer. 'Is that dish low in fat?' gets you a guess from someone who has not seen the recipe.
Know what 'lightly oiled' means before you accept it. In most kitchens it is a tablespoon or two, which is 14 to 28 grams. If you want none, the word to use is none.
Order the kid's portion or the senior portion when there is one. Portion control is fat control, and it is the easiest lever you have that requires nothing from the kitchen.
Two appetizers often make a better meal than an entree. The portions are smaller, and the plain grilled and steamed things tend to live on that part of the menu anyway.
Ask for the box when the food arrives, not when you are finished. Boxing half up front makes the decision once instead of making it again with every bite.
Look up the nutrition information before you go. Chains publish it, it is usually accurate, and deciding at home in a quiet room is easier than deciding at the table with everyone waiting.
Call ahead during a slow hour. Kitchens are dramatically more accommodating at 3pm than at 7pm, and a chef who has already agreed on the phone is an ally when you arrive.
If the answer is no, order plain and move on. A baked potato, plain rice, a broth soup, and a salad with vinegar is a real meal, it is available almost everywhere, and it is a fine thing to eat.
Alcohol is the one item on any menu with no modified version. Everything else has one.
universal.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could you ask the kitchen to prepare mine with no butter and no oil, using broth or a light spray if they need something, and bring any sauce or dressing on the side?

cuisines.label: American
safeBets: Grilled chicken breast, plain, with a baked potato and a vegetable that has not met butter
Roast turkey with the gravy on the side
A broth based soup, vegetable or chicken noodle, once you have confirmed it is not a cream base
Garden salad with balsamic or red wine vinegar in place of a creamy dressing
Grilled fish with lemon, and a shrimp cocktail as a starter
avoid: Anything fried, crispy, breaded, or battered, which is usually half the menu
Burgers, and especially anything described as a double, a stack, or loaded
Potato skins, cheese fries, spinach dip, and the rest of the shared appetizer page
Ranch, blue cheese, Caesar, and thousand island dressings
Alcohol, which is the one thing here with no modified version
askFor: Sauce, gravy, and dressing on the side
The vegetables steamed with nothing on them, and the potato plain
The chicken cooked dry, or with broth instead of oil
A lunch portion, or a box brought out with the plate
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could the kitchen cook the chicken with no oil or butter, steam the vegetables with nothing on them, and bring any sauce on the side?

cuisines.label: Italian
safeBets: Pasta with marinara, no meat and no cheese, and ask them to skip the oil they finish it with
Grilled chicken or grilled fish with a side of plain vegetables
Minestrone or pasta e fagioli, once you have confirmed it is broth based and not cream
Chicken piccata made with lemon and broth rather than butter, if the kitchen will do it that way
Plain bread with no oil dish, and a salad with vinegar
avoid: Alfredo, carbonara, vodka sauce, and anything the menu calls creamy
Fried calamari, arancini, and mozzarella sticks
Anything parmigiana, which is breaded, fried, and then covered in cheese
Pesto, which is mostly olive oil and pine nuts even when it looks like a vegetable
Sausage, pancetta, and prosciutto cooked into a sauce, where the fat is invisible
The oil at the table and the wine list, neither of which has a modified version
askFor: Marinara in place of any cream sauce, and no finishing oil on the pasta
No cheese on top, and none brought to the table
A lunch portion, a half order, or an appetizer portion of the pasta
The vegetables steamed rather than sauteed
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could you ask the kitchen to prepare the chicken with no oil or butter, use marinara rather than any cream sauce, skip the cheese, and bring the sauce on the side?

cuisines.label: Mexican
safeBets: Chicken or shrimp fajitas cooked with no oil, on soft corn tortillas
Whole black beans or whole pinto beans in place of refried
Grilled chicken or grilled fish tacos, soft shell
Salsa, pico de gallo, and hot sauce, all of which are essentially fat free and do most of the flavor work
Plain rice, grilled vegetables, and a side of lime
avoid: Refried beans, which are traditionally cooked with lard
Cheese, queso, sour cream, and guacamole, which are where the fat actually is
Chimichangas, chile rellenos, taquitos, and anything else out of the fryer
The chip basket, which is fried and very hard to stop eating once it is in front of you
Carnitas, chorizo, and barbacoa, all of which are fatty cuts by design
Margaritas and beer, which have no modified version
askFor: The meat and the fajita vegetables cooked with no oil, or on a dry flat top
No cheese, no sour cream, and no guacamole, with extra pico and salsa instead
Whole beans rather than refried
Corn tortillas rather than a fried shell or a fried bowl
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could the kitchen cook the chicken and vegetables with no oil, and leave off the cheese, sour cream, and guacamole? Extra salsa and pico de gallo would be great.

cuisines.label: Chinese
safeBets: Steamed chicken or steamed shrimp with vegetables, sauce on the side
Steamed white or brown rice
Wonton soup or hot and sour soup, in a small bowl
Moo goo gai pan, or any steamed vegetable dish with the sauce served separately
Steamed dumplings rather than fried, in a small portion
avoid: General Tso's, sesame chicken, orange chicken, sweet and sour, and anything the menu calls crispy
Egg rolls, spring rolls, crab rangoon, and fried wontons
Fried rice and lo mein, both of which are cooked in a real quantity of oil
Duck, spare ribs, and dishes built around cashews or peanuts
askFor: The dish steamed rather than stir fried, with the sauce on the side
No oil in the wok, or a dry wok if they are able
Steamed rice in place of fried rice
A small portion, or a box brought with the meal
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I get the chicken and vegetables steamed rather than stir fried, with the sauce on the side and steamed rice?

cuisines.label: Japanese
safeBets: Sashimi and simple nigiri, which are among the leanest things you can order in any restaurant
Edamame, steamed, with no butter
Miso soup, seaweed salad, and a cucumber roll
Chicken teriyaki with the sauce on the side
Steamed rice, and a plain vegetable roll
avoid: Tempura and anything else that arrives in a batter
Spicy mayo, eel sauce, and any roll described as dynamite, crunchy, or creamy
Katsu, which is breaded and fried
Fatty tuna, sold as toro, and large portions of salmon, which carries real fat even though it is good fat
askFor: No spicy mayo and no crunchy topping on any roll
The teriyaki sauce on the side
Steamed rice rather than fried rice
Grilled rather than tempura or katsu
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the chicken grilled with the teriyaki sauce on the side, and no spicy mayo or crunchy topping on anything?

cuisines.label: Indian
safeBets: Tandoori chicken or tandoori fish, which is cooked dry in a very hot oven
Chicken tikka, meaning the dry version rather than tikka masala
Plain basmati rice
Dal, once you have confirmed it was not finished with ghee or cream
Tandoori roti or plain naan rather than butter naan
Raita made with low fat yogurt, and the chutneys, most of which carry no fat at all
avoid: Korma, tikka masala, butter chicken, and anything else in a cream or coconut base
Samosas, pakoras, and bhaji, all of which are deep fried
Paneer, which is a full fat fresh cheese however gently it is cooked
Butter naan, garlic naan, and paratha, which are layered with fat as they are made
Ghee anywhere it appears, including brushed on bread at the end
askFor: Tandoori rather than any curry with a cream base
The dish made with no ghee, no cream, and no coconut milk
A tomato based sauce rather than a cream based one, when the kitchen offers both
Plain rice and plain roti, with nothing brushed on
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the tandoori chicken with no ghee brushed on it, plain rice, and plain roti rather than butter naan?

cuisines.label: Thai
safeBets: Tom yum soup, which is broth based, rather than tom kha, which is coconut milk
Steamed rice with grilled chicken or grilled shrimp
Larb or green papaya salad, both dressed with lime and fish sauce rather than oil
Steamed vegetables with the sauce served on the side
Basil chicken, asked for with very little oil
avoid: Anything built on coconut milk, which means most of the curries, green, red, yellow, massaman, and panang
Pad thai, which carries oil, egg, and crushed peanuts together
Fried spring rolls, crab rangoon, and fried tofu
Peanut sauce and satay
Anything described as crispy
askFor: A broth base rather than a coconut base
Steamed, or cooked with very little oil, with the sauce on the side
No peanuts and no peanut sauce
Mild rather than hot, since very spicy food is uncomfortable for a lot of people while they are recovering
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the chicken and vegetables steamed or cooked with very little oil, no coconut milk, no peanuts, and the sauce on the side?

cuisines.label: Mediterranean
safeBets: Grilled chicken or grilled fish souvlaki with no oil brushed on
Chicken shawarma, which is considerably leaner than the lamb or the gyro cone
Plain rice pilaf and grilled vegetables
Greek salad with no feta and no olives, dressed with lemon and red wine vinegar
Lentil soup or avgolemono, once you have confirmed the base
Tzatziki made with low fat yogurt, in a small amount
avoid: Gyro meat and lamb, both of which are high fat before anything is added
Falafel, which is deep fried however green it looks
Hummus and baba ganoush in any real quantity, since both are built on tahini and oil
Feta, olives, and the olive oil poured over almost everything at the end
Spanakopita and baklava, which are layered with butter
askFor: The meat grilled with no oil brushed on before or after
No feta, no olives, and no oil on the salad
Lemon and vinegar in place of dressing
Pita plain rather than brushed and grilled
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the chicken grilled with no oil brushed on, a salad with no feta or olives and just lemon on it, and plain rice?

cuisines.label: Diner
safeBets: Grilled chicken sandwich on a dry bun with mustard in place of mayonnaise
Turkey sandwich on plain bread with lettuce, tomato, and mustard
A broth based soup with crackers
Baked potato with salsa or salt, and a side salad with vinegar
Grilled chicken over a salad with the dressing on the side
avoid: Everything out of the fryer, which at a diner is fries, rings, mozzarella sticks, and most of the appetizers
Melts, clubs, and anything that arrives with mayonnaise already on it
Gravy, biscuits, and anything country fried
Milkshakes and pie
askFor: No butter on the bun and no butter on the grill
Mustard in place of mayonnaise
A side salad or fruit in place of the fries
Dressing and gravy on the side
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I get the grilled chicken with no butter on the grill or the bun, mustard instead of mayonnaise, and a side salad instead of fries?

cuisines.label: Fast food
safeBets: Grilled chicken sandwich with no mayonnaise and no cheese
A plain single hamburger with mustard and ketchup
Grilled chicken wrap or salad with the dressing on the side
Apple slices, a side salad, or a plain baked potato where they have one
Chili in a small size, at the places that make it
avoid: Anything fried, which is most of the menu at most of these places
Cheese, bacon, mayonnaise, and special sauce, which is where nearly all of the fat lives
Anything sized up, doubled, or described as loaded
Milkshakes, frozen coffee drinks, and fried pies
askFor: No mayonnaise, no cheese, and no special sauce
Grilled rather than crispy
The smallest size, or the kid's meal, which is a real portion
A side salad or fruit in place of the fries
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the grilled chicken sandwich with no mayonnaise, no cheese, and no special sauce?

cuisines.label: Steakhouse
safeBets: Filet or sirloin, the smallest cut on the menu, trimmed, with no butter finish
Grilled chicken or grilled fish, which most steakhouses do very well and rarely get ordered
Shrimp cocktail, which is lean, and the cocktail sauce carries no fat
Plain baked potato and steamed vegetables with nothing on them
Side salad with vinegar, dressing on the side
avoid: Ribeye, prime rib, porterhouse, and anything the menu calls marbled
The butter finish, which most steakhouses add by default and almost never mention
Creamed spinach, loaded potatoes, and macaroni and cheese
Bread with butter, and the giant fried onion appetizer
Bearnaise, hollandaise, and any compound or blue cheese butter
askFor: No butter on the steak, which is the one that has to be said out loud every time
The smallest cut, the 6 ounce rather than the 12
The potato plain, with nothing on it and nothing alongside it
Vegetables steamed with no butter
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the smallest sirloin, trimmed, with no butter on it at all, a plain baked potato with nothing on it, and steamed vegetables with no butter?

cuisines.label: Seafood
safeBets: Grilled, baked, or broiled white fish, cooked with lemon and broth in place of butter
Steamed shrimp, steamed crab legs, or a shrimp cocktail, with cocktail sauce rather than drawn butter
Steamed clams or mussels in a broth, once you have confirmed it is not a butter or cream broth
Plain rice, a plain baked potato, or steamed vegetables
A broth based seafood soup rather than a chowder
avoid: The fried half of the menu, which at most seafood places is the larger half
Drawn butter, which is about 11 grams a tablespoon and arrives without anyone asking for it
Chowder and bisque, both of which are cream based
Crab cakes and stuffed fish, usually bound with mayonnaise or butter
Blackened, which in most kitchens means dredged in butter before it hits the pan
askFor: Broiled dry, with lemon and broth in place of butter
No drawn butter, and none brought to the table
Old Bay, lemon, vinegar, or cocktail sauce for flavor
Steamed rather than fried, which every seafood kitchen can do
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could the kitchen broil the fish dry with lemon and no butter at all, and bring no drawn butter to the table?

cuisines.label: Breakfast
safeBets: Egg whites or an egg white omelet cooked with spray rather than butter
Oatmeal made with water or skim milk, with fruit on it
Dry toast or an English muffin with jam in place of butter
A small stack of plain pancakes with syrup rather than butter
Fresh fruit, and yogurt when it is a nonfat one
Turkey bacon or Canadian bacon in a small portion
avoid: Bacon, sausage, biscuits, and gravy, which is most of what a breakfast menu is built on
Home fries and hash browns, both cooked on a well greased flat top
Anything described as loaded, stuffed, or a skillet
Croissants, danishes, and buttered toast
Cream cheese, which is very nearly all fat
askFor: Egg whites cooked with cooking spray, no butter and no cream added
Dry toast, which in a kitchen means no butter on it at all
Fruit in place of the potatoes
Syrup on the side rather than butter on top
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have an egg white omelet cooked with spray and no butter or cream, dry toast with no butter, and fruit instead of the potatoes?

cuisines.label: Barbecue
safeBets: Smoked turkey breast, or smoked chicken breast with the skin removed
Pulled chicken with a vinegar based or tomato based sauce
The lean end of the brisket rather than the point, in a small portion
Green beans, collards, or vegetables cooked without fatback, when the kitchen makes them that way
Vinegar slaw rather than creamy slaw, and corn on the cob with no butter
avoid: Ribs, burnt ends, sausage links, and pork belly
The point end of the brisket, which is the fatty half of the same cut
Macaroni and cheese, baked beans made with bacon, and creamy coleslaw
Cornbread, which is usually built on butter or bacon fat
White sauce and any mayonnaise based sauce
askFor: The lean end of the brisket, sliced, with the fat cap trimmed off
Sauce on the side, and a vinegar or tomato based one rather than a creamy one
Chicken breast with the skin removed
A sandwich portion rather than a plate, or a box brought with the plate
cuisines.scriptLine: I have a medical condition that requires a very low fat diet. Could I have the sliced turkey or the lean end of the brisket with the fat trimmed, sauce on the side, and no butter on the vegetables?
